Subject: Entitlement exception request — PulseShift Labs (VP/CFO sign-off required)

Team — opening a quick thread for an upcoming renewal negotiation that needs an entitlement/seat-mix exception and VP/CFO sign-off. Summary: PulseShift Labs (early-stage genomics tooling) is asking to convert a hosted usage commitment into a mixed entitlement that includes 50 reserved vCPU-equivalent seats plus a soft usage buffer for inference. They are at a $450k ARR commitment today and want a 28% one-time onboarding discount off list for the first 12 months to support a multi-region POC and private VPC connectivity.

Why this is different: the ask combines a high-percentage onboarding discount with a seat-floor reduction for the first six months and guaranteed access to dedicated burst capacity in our East region. Finance flags: this pushes projected unit economics ~18% below our typical high-touch starter profile. Strategic rationale: PulseShift is a high-visibility reference in genomic research (they have NIH grants) and could justify prioritizing a VPC region for us — long-term upside.

Request: seeking approval for the following exception scope to present to the customer: 1) 28% on onboarding for months 1–12 (one-time invoice credit), 2) seat-floor at 50 seats vs. 75 standard starter, 3) guaranteed burst agreement (up to 6 vGPU-hours/day) for first 90 days, 4) milestone-based clawback if usage/commitment < 30% after month 6.

Attachments: I attached the SOW draft and a pricing model (pulseshift-pricing-model.xlsx) with P&L impact.

Next steps I'd like: Marissa/Kimberly — can you confirm commercial framing and suggested guardrails? Markus — if this looks directionally ok, would appreciate a quick greenlight or a call. Eli from PulseShift is pushing for commercial terms this week (their board meets Friday).

Thanks,
Dev
Dev Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

- 28% one-time onboarding credit is high; recommend we propose a tiered onboarding credit: 20% upfront + additional 8% tied to the POC milestone being signed off at day 90. That preserves a partial clawback incentive.
- Seat-floor at 50 is acceptable if we get a hard commit to minimum monthly spend (add to SOW).
- Burst access should be timeboxed and usage-metered; legal needs the SLA language.

Quick financials after running Dev's model:
- Base list for the proposed bundle (50-seat mix + soft buffer) = $620k ARR annualized.
- Proposed blended effective price with 28% onboarding credit = ~$446k ARR first year (with the credit recognized over the first invoice).
- Trailing twelve-month unit margin drops from our target 38% to ~21% in year one under straight 28%.

Recommendation
- Acceptable path: 20% upfront onboarding credit + 8% contingent tied to POC milestone (net 28% if milestone met).
- Add a 6-month review clause: if realized usage < 30% of expected ARR at month 6, then a pro-rated clawback or future invoice offset replicating the percentage shortfall.
- Cap total enterprise concessions to ensure lifetime margin floor: propose maximum cumulative concession not to exceed $120k NPV.

Operational ask: Legal to add explicit burst access window (90 days) and a measurement clause; Ops to confirm we can reserve East-region capacity for their POC dates (target start 2026-06-08).

Attachments: summarized pricing worksheet (pulseshift-pricing-model.xlsx).

Kimberly Park
Director, Revenue Strategy — Redwood Inference
